title: Raise check timeout to 1800s; hold timed-out checks; report in status
summary: Retry of job 20261029-084645-sza7, which was rejected because the reading deferred part (3) of the request. Goal: the maintainer stops random rejections from killed test checks. This reading does all three parts: check_timeout_s = 1800, a timed-out check becomes an environment stop (held and retried) with its duration against the limit printed, and athena status reports median and slowest test-check durations with an 80% flag.

defaults_applied.how: Criteria check the end state of a timed-out job and what status prints, not that wiring exists.
New tests plus fmt, clippy -D warnings and the full test suite.
Fake-runner tests assert the job end state for a timeout and for a real failure.
CHANGELOG entry written for outside readers, citing the job.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: read crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs (check_timeout_s used at lines ~819, 1107, 1395, 1844; check_and_verify), crates/athena-core/src/disk.rs (is_environment_reason line 212, resumable_stop line 221), crates/athena-data/src/config.rs (check_timeout_s: u64 at line 234, schema unchanged). No new record or data file is added, so no check_record_file/AnyRecord change; the status report is computed from existing stored check records.

Job 20261029-084645-sza7 is addressed as follows. Its candidate (kept as the starting design, redone from base): shared deadline note in checks.rs, a CHECK_TIMEOUT reason in disk.rs, and an early environment-stop return in run/mod.rs, plus the 1800 value and a CHANGELOG entry. Its major finding (part 3 omitted, athena status report missing) is fixed by adding status.rs work now. Its minor finding (a timeout in one check hides a real failure in another) is fixed: hold only when every failed check timed out, else reject. Its minor finding (no check record kept for the timed-out job) is fixed if the existing record structure allows it, otherwise the duration and limit stay in the closing reason.
Environment stop means the existing environment-reason path used for low disk (disk::is_environment_reason, resumable_stop): the job is held and retried, not rejected.
Status durations come from stored test-check run durations of the last 20 jobs; jobs without one are skipped, and with none the report says so rather than showing zero.

acceptance_criteria.text: Grep athena.toml shows check_timeout_s = 1800, and crates/athena-data/src/config.rs still declares check_timeout_s: u64 with its validation unchanged.

Run cargo test --locked: a test with a fake check runner whose check is killed at its deadline (exit code None, deadline note) shows the job closes as an environment stop (disk::is_environment_reason true, resumable_stop true), not Rejected.

Run cargo test --locked: a companion test shows a check failing with a real nonzero exit code is still a failed check that leads to rejection. Another test shows a run where one check timed out and another failed for real is still rejected.
Run cargo test --locked: a test shows the timeout stop reason and printed line contain the measured duration and the limit (for example '905s of 900s limit').

Run cargo test --locked: a status test with seeded jobs shows athena status prints the median and slowest test-check durations over the last 20 jobs against the limit, and flags the slowest when it exceeds 80% of the limit and not when under.
crates/athena-core/src/disk.rs recognises the check-timeout reason in is_environment_reason, with a unit test in the same file.
Run cargo test --locked: the repository config test that loads athena.toml passes with 1800.
Run cargo fmt --all --check, cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings and cargo test --locked: all pass.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry describing the 1800 s limit, timeout-as-environment-stop and the status durations report, citing job 20261026-232434-6wfq.

out_of_scope: Changing the schema or validation of check_timeout_s in crates/athena-data/src/config.rs
Speeding up the test suite or changing reader, producer or verifier timeouts
Adding new fields to CheckRun or other records
departures: Larger than the reference: the change touches five files and includes a status report plus a full-suite verifier run.
urgent_reason: Cuts wasted time from jobs rejected after a timeout kill, which forces redo-work retries.
hard_reason: Changes how a killed check is judged in the run pipeline (rejected vs held environment stop) and so can refuse or hold jobs.
